Game concept for Alchemy Bake Lab, Katy TX · draft for Kady Miller

Sugar Alchemist

A bakery time-management game in the spirit of Papa's Pizzeria, made for Alchemy Bake Lab. Take the order, mix it in the flask, bake, frost, add the sparkle and serve. Every station is scored against the ticket.

Play one day

A rough taste of the first version: mini cupcakes, three customers, the Haunted Lab season. Works with a mouse, touch, or the keyboard (hold Space for the "hold" buttons).

Haunted Lab
Day 1 · Customer 1 of 3Tips $0

How the full game works

The same structure Kady likes from Papa's Pizzeria (tickets, stations, scores, tips, regulars, holiday events), made entirely of Alchemy Bake Lab's own look and treats. No names, art or characters from Papa's.

OrderCustomer reads the order; you pin the ticket. Scored on speed.
Flask labPick the batter, stir until the bubbles turn green.
OvenPull the tray when it's golden. More trays later.
FrostingPick the buttercream and pipe to the line.
Sparkle barGold glitter, cocoa dust, sprinkles, minis, drizzle.
Box & servePack a branded mini treat box. Tip time.

Tokens, next to their rewards

They already use inKind for rewards and Square for payments, so the game sits beside those instead of replacing them:

  • A QR code on the receipt or treat box adds game tokens.
  • Tokens buy extra game days and decor for your own lab.
  • Free play every day; nothing to buy with money; no random prize boxes.
  • Any real prize (like a free mini cupcake for the month's top score) is Kady's call.

Your lab (build mode)

Tips buy decor for your own Alchemy-style lab, built with the engine's building tools and based on their real shop:

  • Black walls, chandeliers, a tufted velvet throne chair
  • Glass cloches, cake stands and macaron towers
  • A neon flask sign that unlocks in magenta, then holographic

Brand guide for development

What you need to know about Alchemy Bake Lab while building the game. All of it is also in the brand kit folder.

Who they are

Alchemy Bake Lab, "Houston's Mini Treat Dealer," a whimsical bakery known for mini desserts, custom cakes and savory minis, with event catering across the Houston area.

Kady Miller started it in 2019 from her home kitchen after being laid off from corporate banking and marketing, grew through COVID-era delivery, and opened the storefront in North Katy. Her team is cross-trained, and the bakery donates to local schools and causes.

Their own line: Whimsical. Edible. Art.

Lettering

Special Elite

The typewriter font on their website, usually in capitals. Station names, tickets, prompts, buttons.

Karla: for anything longer than a label, like instructions and descriptions.

Their website's body font.

Logo

White line art: a round flask holding a steaming pie, a sparkle, green bubbles rising from the top, and the name curved around the bottom in typewriter capitals.

Always on black. Ask Kady for vector files before anything goes public. The kit has a high-resolution PNG and a transparent version.

Voice: keep it family-friendly

Their website is cheeky and grown-up. The game keeps the attitude with kid-safe words. Agree on these with Kady.

On their siteIn the game
"Badass bat shaped Oreos"Bat cookies
"Blackberry absinthe cupcakes"Blackberry potion cupcakes
"Dessert porn" (gallery title)Not used
"Mini Treat Dealer"Ask Kady; "Mini Treat Master" is safe
"Vampire blood," "poison apple"Fine for Halloween

What they already use

  • Square runs their website, online orders and payments.
  • inKind is their rewards app; their site offers $20 toward a $60+ visit for signing up.
  • An email list they call a dessert club, with VIP access.
  • A new catering menu every month, posted as image flyers.

Ask Kady

  • OK to use the logo, name and photos in the game?
  • Which menu words are fine for kids?
  • Which treats should the game help sell?
  • How should game tokens sit next to inKind?
